earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only Lewis 2013 'North Edoid relations and roots' (comparative wordlist) and Ethnologue; no descriptive phonology of Igwe.

sources.citation: Olaogun, Simeon & Oluwaseun Oyelade. 2025. Negation, Tense and Aspect in North-Western Edoid. Beyond Babel: BU Journal of Language, Literature and Humanities 9(1): 370-381. doi:10.5281/zenodo.17129287
sources.note: Nothing on Igwe. Morphosyntax of negation/TAM in Abesabesi and Osse lects with tone-marked data; no prosodic statement transferable to Igwe. PDF not kept (other languages); text extract left in the work dir only.

sources.citation: Rolle, Nicholas. 2026. Tone diachrony beyond tonogenesis: Reconstructing the tone melodies of nouns in Proto-Edoid (Niger-Congo). lingbuzz/009572 v3, forthcoming in Diachronica.
sources.note: Family-wide tone database (40 sources, 21 Edoid languages); footnote: 'The Edoid languages not surveyed in this paper are Ikhin-Arokho [ikh], Enwan [env], Ikpeshi [ikp], Igwe [igw], Sasaru [sxs], Iyayu [iya], Akuku [ayk], and Okpe [okx]' -- confirms no tone-marked Igwe description is available even to a 2026 survey. Nothing on Igwe stress.

sources.citation: Schaefer, Ronald P. & Francis O. Egbokhare. 2021. Edo North: Refugium and micro-accretion zone. Abstract, SLE 2021.
sources.note: Regional generalisation only: 'Tone systems contrast high vs. low, with downstep addition in more southerly areas and mid tone west of center.' Igwe not named; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020 [ed. IV]. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Entry 409 Sasaru-Enwan-Igwe: Edo State, Akoko-Edo LGA; 3,775 (1952); Benue-Congo: Edoid: North-Central Edoid ii; dialects Enwan, Igwe, Sasaru; 'Refs. Comparative: Elugbe (1989)' only -- no phonology or grammar reference exists for the cluster.

sources.citation: Lewis, Demola. 2018. Linguistic prehistory and identity in Nigeria's Bini-Ife pre-eminence contestation. Multilingual Margins 5(1): 2-23. Bellville: Centre for Multilingualism and Diversities Research, University of the Western Cape.
sources.note: No statement on the Igwe tone system or on stress. Igwe content = tone-marked lexical items in the comparative Edoid-Yoruboid tables (e.g. 'fish' Igwe ìɡɛ́nàkpè; 'rope' wúìrì / úrì; 'flower' ūdōdó; Table 4 Igwe Sale numerals ɔ̄ːwò '1', īɡbé '10', úwòhē '20', ɔ́ɡbã̀ '30', addition 11-15, subtraction 16-19, vigesimal 40/60) carrying three tone diacritics (acute, macron, grave) plus nasalization -- wordlist-type data only -- and a few sentences of segmental diachronic commentary ('The extant Igwe form ìɡɛ́nàkpè stands out first as the etymon of the word fish in Edoid, where the consonant on the…

sources.citation: Ethnologue 19 (Lewis, Simons & Fennig 2016), 'Igwe' [igw] public page (the Internet Archive copy)
sources.note: 'Population 47,800 (2000). Location Edo state: Akoko-Edo LGA. Language Status 6a (Vigorous). Classification.. Edoid, North-Central, Ghotuo-Uneme-Yekhee.' No alternate names, dialects or language resources listed; nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Lewis, 'Demola. 2016. A Leipzig-Jakarta Vocabulary Reconstruction and Sound Correspondence based Sub-grouping of North Edoid. Abstract with data appendices (16 pp; Table 1 + 'Leipzig-Jakarta list (North Western Edoid)' and '(North Central Edoid)'), 2nd International Congress 'Towards Proto-Niger-Congo: Comparison and Reconstruction', Paris, 1-3 September 2016. Paris: LLACAN.
sources.note: No prose on prosody. The Igwe forms are transcribed with lexical tone diacritics (acute, grave and macron, e.g. item 10 'blood' Igwe-Sale ɔ̀rà, Igwe-Oke ɔ̄rá; item 2 'arm/hand' óbɔ̀ / ītʃágūā), i.e. the author treats Igwe as a tone language with at least H, M(macron), L marks, but states nothing about the tone system, and nothing about stress.

sources.citation: Lewis, Demola. 2015. Deciphering Aborigines and Migrants from Cognation and Topography in North-Western Edo. Lengua y Migracion 7(1): 29-51.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Lexicostatistics only: Table 2b 'Igwe Cognation across Owan' (62-63% with Eese and Ihievbe, 43-52% with the rest); Table 5 'Cognation Percentages for Igwe Sale-Sasaru-Enwa' (Enwa-Igwe c. 50%); 'the Igwe are returnee immigrants' from Akoko-Edo into north-western Owan; fn.2: 'Igwe, Uokha Arokho and Ake all belong to the same migrant party comprising a language cluster. However, Igwe aligns with Ghotou in certain lexical items due to contact.'

sources.citation: Egbokhare, Francis O. 2011. The Sound of Meaning. Inaugural lecture, University of Ibadan.
sources.note: Igwe appears only in Oyakhire's (1997) Owan mutual-intelligibility groups, 'E: Igwe, Ikao, Otuo' (p.69), and in the list of villages where Northern-Edo project audio tapes were recorded. Table 8 'Linguistic Features of NCE and NWE' (tone systems 2 / 2+DS / 3) has no Igwe row. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Pogoson, Ohioma I. & Francis O. Egbokhare (eds.). 2002. New Perspectives in Edoid Studies: Essays in Honour of Ronald Peter Schaefer (CASAS Book Series 20). Cape Town: Centre for Advanced Studies of African Society. ISBN 1-919799-68-0. [154-pp scan in the University of Ibadan repository, handle 123456789/5455]
sources.note: No phonology content for Igwe. The one North-Edo linguistic chapter (Pogoson & Egbokhare, pp.16-34, scanned in full) restates Elugbe's (1986/1989) Edoid family tree and lexicostatistic/glottochronological reasoning about Benin-origin traditions; Igwe/Igue is not named; the words tone/stress occur only in non-linguistic senses. Image-only 45.7 MB scan: TOC + this chapter scanned (26 pages), extract kept, big file deleted.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohi. 1989. Edoid. In John Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo Languages, 291-304. Lanham: University Press of America. (Zenodo 5618102)
sources.note: Igwe appears only as item 'h) Igwe' in the NCE classification list (pp.296-297). Sec. 13.3.4 'Tone systems' (pp.298-299) surveys Degema, Egene, Eruwa, Isoko, Edo, Ghotuo, Oloma, Ibilo, Emhalhe -- no Igwe, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohiomamhe. 1989. Comparative Edoid: Phonology and Lexicon (Delta Series 6). Port Harcourt: University of Port Harcourt Press. xvii+253 pp. (Zenodo 5688969, CC-BY)
sources.note: Nothing for Igwe. Igwe is named only on pp.10-11 ('Igwe and Ihievbe (Sebe) of Owan' among clans 'most likely North-Central Edoid peoples') and in the classification list p.24 '(h) Igwe-Enwa-Sasaru', with the footnote that g-i 'are left out of the family tree because their exact relationship with the rest of NCE has not been determined'. No Igwe sketch, no Igwe forms in the lexicon (Glottolog langnote: 'Mentions.. Igwe [igw].. but without data'). The word 'stress' does not occur in the text.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid igwe1238 (JSON), Wikidata Q3913985, en.wikipedia 'Igwe language' and 'Edoid languages', ISO 639-3 igw record, Joshua Project igw, local Glottolog hh.bib
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description = Lewis 2013 'a wordlist or less'; hh.bib carries [igw] only in the Elugbe 1989 langnote ('without data') and the Lewis 2013 language code ('Igwe-Sale = Igwe [igw], Igwe Oke = Igwe [igw]'). Wikipedia 'Edoid languages' reproduces 12 tone-marked wordlist items each for 'Igwe (Sale)' and 'Igwe (Oke)' attributed to Lewis (2013), showing that the thesis holds tone-marked Igwe wordlists; no prose on tone or stress.
